column1: # Every function of the node source that reads the bytes of a secret (rule E2 of the egress
# policy, docs/egress-policy.md). `scripts/secret-access.sh --check` compares the first three
# columns with the source and fails when a function is missing here or no longer exists.
# Columns, separated by tabs: file, function, uses of `expose_secret` in it (for
# protocol/src/secret.rs: uses of the private fields), use, note.
# use: K1 record ciphertext, K2 seal to a verified peer, K3 TLS connection to a provider,
# K4 vault value of `release`, K5 TLS connection to the log store, K6 and K7 TLS connection to
# a mail endpoint, K8 seal to a verified node of the forward role, K9 TLS connection to the
# site of a vault secret, in-node (the result stays inside the node or is a signature, a
# ciphertext or a public key), declassify (the result leaves in the clear and is one of the

column5: the value of a secret use as it is written inside a header value: the result is a secret
the value of a secret use percent-encoded for a path, a query parameter or a form field: the result is a secret
the value of a secret use as the content of a JSON string: the result is a secret
a text of the caller with the written value in the place of its one placeholder: the result is a secret
the bytes of a written value as text, for a header value and for the request target: the result is a secret
one bit: whether the value of an opened envelope can stand inside a header value or as the half of the credentials of HTTP Basic its slot names (the refusal invalid_request of vault/send)
the length of a request body the node assembled, for the Content-Length of the request to the provider
the length of a header value, for the length of the head of a request: a connection that carried a head above a bound is not kept for a further request
the length of a request body with the value of a secret use in it, for the Content-Length of the request to the site
writes the request target, a header value and the body with the value of a secret use into the one request of its envelope, which goes to the site of that envelope over TLS
writes a secret header value and a secret body into the request that goes to the provider over TLS

signs a request to the log store with AWS Signature Version 4: the session token of the operator is one of the signed headers, and its secret access key is the key of the HMAC chain. What leaves is the signature, in the request that goes to the log store over TLS. Neither value is a secret of an account
writes the session token of the operator into a header of the request that goes to the log store over TLS

parses the opened plaintext of a mail record into the private mail credential type, after the log store confirmed the entry of the call: the result is a secret, and the refusal record_invalid of a plaintext the call cannot use leaves with that entry
authenticates only to imap.naver.com over in-node TLS
authenticates only to smtp.naver.com over in-node TLS

the length of the token of a forward request: the share of the body budget the call holds for its credential, which is what the search of the response can hold and the copies of the token the request carries. The sizes of the parts of a stream follow that length as well (docs/egress-policy.md section 5, side channels)
encodes 32 random bytes as the verifier text: the result is a secret
the S256 challenge of the verifier, part of the authorization address

counts the arrays, objects and commas of the opened plaintext of a token record, and parses the plaintext when its parsed form stays within the room of a token object: the result is a secret, or the outcome of a check
a token response becomes the plaintext of a record: the result is a secret
the lengths of the tokens of a plaintext, for the bound of the token a node handles: the outcome of a check
the refresh rule over two secrets: the result is a secret
the reconnect rule over two secrets: the result is a secret
the refresh token for a token request: the result is a secret
the token for a revocation request: the result is a secret
the token and the header value (the prefix and the token, or HTTP Basic of the rule's user name and the token) of a forward request: all results are secrets
the client id a record holds, for a token or revocation request: the result is a secret
the public fields of rule E4: the listed leaves, the time the token was obtained, one bit for the refresh token, or the refusal response_withheld
serializes the plaintext for record::seal, and judges its length and the room of its parsed form by the bounds of a record a node reads: the bytes leave as the ciphertext of a record, or not at all
the length of a value, for the size of the buffer the form body is written into
writes the secret values into the form body of a token or revocation request: the body is a secret
writes the secret values into the JSON body of a token request: the body is a secret
the HTTP Basic header value of a token or revocation request: the result is a secret

of an accepted token response nothing: what the node keeps of it stays a secret, and the strings it leaves out end with the parsed response. Of a refused one, and of one above the bounds of a node (the room of its parsed form, the length of a token, the room of what the node would keep of it), the HTTP status and one word of the closed vocabulary of rule E5
the encoded forms of a credential for the search: each form is a secret

the length of the longest form of a credential: how many bytes of a body the search of a stream holds back. The sizes of the parts of a stream follow that number; the length of a credential is what the size of its request to the provider shows as well (docs/egress-policy.md section 5, side channels)

the searchers of the forms of a credential, each of which borrows its form. What the search gives out is one bit: whether bytes a provider or a site sent hold a credential (the refusal response_withheld)
the forms of a credential with their ASCII letters in lower case, for the search of a header name, which the HTTP client hands on in lower case: each form is a secret
two random values become the private keys of the node

the name, the sites, the slots and the source of the plaintext of a vault_secret record, read without decoding its value: the reach decides the refusal not_allowed, and the name goes into the event of the call, which is sealed to the log key of the account
parses a vault plaintext and takes the string of one member, after the entry of the call is confirmed: the result is a secret, or the refusal record_invalid
a vault value, or the TOTP code computed from the seed, becomes part of the response of release, as it is or under the seal of the key the call named, after its log entry

judges the value of a use after its log entry (8 to 12,000 bytes, and no control character where its slot is a header or a half of the credentials of HTTP Basic: the refusal record_invalid) and hands it to the seal for the verified node of the forward role
the plaintext of a vault_secret record of a value the caller of vault/store gave: the result is a secret
the plaintext of a vault_password record of a value the caller of vault/store gave: the result is a secret
serializes that plaintext and holds it to the limit of 12,272 bytes (the refusal too_large of a value the caller gave): the result is a secret
the public parts of a grant or a revoke command (user_id, challenge, sign_pk, log_pk, custody, not_after_ms). The user key becomes a secret
user keys go into the payload of a delegation transfer: the payload is a secret
signs the transfer payload and seals it to the sealing key of the verified peer
the public parts of the grants of a transfer (user_id, sign_pk, log_pk, custody, not_after_ms). The user keys become secrets
the key material of the HPKE seal of a log entry of format 1
the key material of the HPKE seal of a log entry of format 2
the key material of the HPKE seal of a log entry of format 3
decrypts a record with the user key: the plaintext is a secret
encrypts a secret plaintext under a key derived from the user key
seals a vault value with HPKE to the key the caller of release named: the ciphertext is the sealed value of the response of release
the credentials of HTTP Basic with the value as the half its slot names, as the base64 text of the Authorization header: the result is a secret

the length of the value of a secret use: the share of the body budget the search of the response to its request can hold. The sizes of the parts of a stream follow that length as well (docs/egress-policy.md section 5, side channels)
the value of a vault secret goes into the payload of a secret use: the payload is a secret
signs the payload of a secret use and seals it to the sealing key of the verified node of the forward role
the public parts of a secret use (the two nodes, the two times, the number of the use, user_id, record_id, the request object): they decide the refusals of vault/send. The value becomes a secret
the accessor itself: its callers are the lines above
creates a secret in place from the random source
copies a key into another secret
overwrites the bytes with zeros
the signing public key of the node
the sealing public key of the node
an Ed25519 signature of the node over a body
an Ed25519 signature of the node over a transfer payload
opens an HPKE seal made to the node: the plaintext is a secret
